LESSON: WRITING 3.5.1 PARAGRAPHING: SEQUENCING OF IDEAS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.5: Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to use conjunctions in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph
2. use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph
3. appreciate the role of conjunctions in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 3.5.1 PARAGRAPHING: SEQUENCING OF IDEAS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 3.5.1 PARAGRAPHING: SEQUENCING OF IDEAS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph

What this means
In this part you learn to identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph

What this means
In this part you learn to use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of conjunctions in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of conjunctions in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of conjunctions in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of conjunctions in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas to a partner. (skill: use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of conjunctions in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph.
3. Practise this skill: use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of conjunctions in communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to use conjunctions in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 3.5.1 Paragraphing: Sequencing of Ideas means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify conjunctions used in a well formed paragraph.
5. Be able to: use conjunctions to sequence and connect ideas correctly in a paragraph.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
